To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the optimum buffer thickness for a given overshoot depends on the sulfur mole fraction and the structure type, and (ii) the optimum overshoot for a given buffer thickness depends on the sulfur composition and the structure type.
“For dislocation compensation in lattice-mismatch heterostructures, the thickness of the buffer layer and the amount of composition overshoot at the interface are both critical design parameters.”

(i) the dislocation density is minimized when the buffer thickness is chosen to be equal to the optimum thickness for the buffer–device interface overshoot that is used in the buffer; (ii) the optimum buffer–device interface overshot is a function of the misfit and the dislocation mobility, and is independent of the buffer thickness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a fundamental understanding of dislocation behavior in lattice-mismatch semiconductor heterostructures, and applying that knowledge to the design of metamorphic heterostructure devices.
the design and analysis of lattice-mismatched metamorphic device structures with low defect density and enhanced performance.
the design of metamorphic heterostructures with reduced dislocations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dislocation-compensating metamorphic buffers are a promising technology for the growth of high-performance and highly reliable lattice-mismatched heterostructures.
for both structure types, there exists a unique combination of buffer thickness and compositional overshoot which minimises the threading dislocation density in the device layer.

for given overshoot at the interface of the buffer and device layers there is an optimum thickness of the buffer layer which minimizes the threading dislocation density and that for given buffer thickness, there is an optimal overshoot that minimizes the dislocations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dislocation-compensating heterostructures with low threading dislocations can be designed for ZnSySe1–y/GaAs structures with a wide range of device layer sulfur mole fractions.
the dislocation density in a dislocation-compensating ZnSySe1–y/GaAs heterostructure can be minimized by optimizing the buffer thickness and the compositional overshoot.
the optimum buffer thickness and overshoot are determined by a balance between minimizing dislocation density and minimizing overshoot.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the tolerance in sulfur mole fraction is significantly larger than previously thought and that the dislocation-compensating mechanism can be used to design metamorphic devices with high performance and reliability.

for a given overshoot tolerance, there is an optimal buffer design which minimizes threading dislocation density and that the tolerance in overshoot is more important than the buffer design for achieving low threading dislocation densities.
the tolerance for compositional overshoot in the buffer is significantly relaxed for type B structures compared to type A structures.
